steps.text: Combine tuna, egg, bread crumbs, onion, celery, red bell pepper, mayonnaise, hot chili sauce, chili sauce, dill, salt, pepper, hot pepper sauce and Worcestershire sauce. Mix well. Shape into 4 patties (mixture will be very soft and delicate). Refrigerate for 30 minutes to make the patties easier to handle, if desired.
Coat a nonstick skillet with cooking spray; fry tuna patties for about 3 to 4 minutes per side, or until cooked through. These are fragile, so be careful when turning them.
Serve on buns with tomato slices and lettuce leaves, if desired.

raw_recipe.headline: Tasty Tuna Burgers
raw_recipe.description: These tuna burgers are so delicious. My husband is a very fussy eater, and he loves these. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody:
My family is out of cash and we have canned tuna specially for these hard times, so making this recipe was perfect. It took 30 minutes to make from start to finish along with cooking baked potatoes. Everyone absolutely loved this recipe and the cost is so low even paupers like me can live like kings. (stomach-wise) hehe

Seriously, this is a lightning fast, budget friendly and super yummy recipe.. it is also very forgiving when you dont have all the ingredients.

Wow these were way better than expected. You’d never know these were made from canned tuna. Very much like a salmon cakes in my opinion. Made exactly as written but when adding an extra large egg it made the mixture too wet and impossible to handle. So instead of adding more bread crumbs I just added another can of tuna and a little extra salt. Worked out perfectly and it made 4 nice sized parties. As others suggested I refrigerated the patties for about 30 minutes before frying. Instead of lettuce and tomato, which I’ll try next time, I topped with a cabbage slaw made with the Cilantro Serrano Cream Sauce also on this site! Yummo!! Hubby really enjoyed them too. Thanks for a fantastic recipe, looking forward to making them again!

These were delicious! I used albacor tuna...made these meaty and delicious! We grilled our patties on a gas grill using a grill pan sprayed with olive oil cooking spray...about 3 minutes each side. We ate these on homemade buns and topped the patties with a special pink sauce (ketchup/mayo mixed together). Almost tasted like a restaurant!

The KEY STEP is in using WHITE CHUNK to have no moisture/wetness problems. I used 2 cans (6 oz or 170 gms) . We didn't have any Italian bread crumbs so used PANKO Japanese style bread crumbs. Increased the mayo to 1/2 cup. Mashed all the tuna up separately before adding all the other ingredients and used the back of a wooden spoon to press down the mix until it was really firm. Put it in the fridge for 30 minutes as suggested and then followed the recipe's instructions. the burgers stayed firm, were easy to turn over and came out A-1. Really tasty. My wife said "that's a keeper". She had hers without the bun and remarked that one could if wished serve them like that with a a side dish (such as garlic shrimp, a veggie and salad

Made exactly to the recipe. After they were slightly browned on both sides, I added a slice of sharp cheddar on top and warmed until melted. Served on toasted potato buns with tomato and lettuce. Very good, and I don’t even like tuna!

These are outstanding! I did not use the dill, pepper sauce or chili sauce. I doubled the recipe then lightly oiled a glass baking dish, and using a round egg chopper, I placed it in the baking dish and filled the center with the mix - making a nice patty. I used the egg chopper to make a total of 5 patties. I put them in the oven set to 400 and let it bake for approximately 30-40 minutes. They tasted wonderful! I served it with cocktail sauce. YUM and easy!

I loved this recipe but I did make some changes:
I put everything in a food processor which made the burger super melt-in-your mouth. I didn't have any of the sauces mentioned on hand so I left them out which worked fine. I used chili pepper, instead. To make it healthier I used plain greek yogurt instead of mayo. I also threw in cumin, smoked paprika, and a little finely chopped jalapeno for some kick. I didn't have celery so I used 1/3 cup corn instead. I used crackers for the breadcrumbs and because it still looked moist after the 1/2 cup I added but I was out of crackers I added in some rolled oats. I refrigerated for about 30 minutes. Just before cooking I mixed in some fresh cilantro. Next time I will puree everything together except for the onions, corn, and bell peppers (If I use them) to add a little texture.

These are delicious! The cilantro aoli with these are a must. The only change I made was using fresh dill, because I love it. We ate the left overs (because I doubled the recipe) as a lettuce wrap for lunch which were also delicious. These are in the regular rotation for weekday dinners because they are quick, easy and delicious.

These were really tasty! I used plain 2% Greek yogurt instead of mayonnaise to reduce calories. I didn’t have any bread crumbs so I used panko instead, and also I reduced the amount of salt by half. I threw the veggies in a chopper and there was a lot of liquid once they were minced, so I pressed as much liquid out as I could before adding the rest of the ingredients. They do have to be handled carefully but they stayed together and were delicious - I will definitely be making these again.

I loved the taste, however was very liquidly. I added a cup more of fresh bread crumbs to absorb the juices, and refrigerated overnight. When I formed the patties, they were more like a runny dough. But, I fried them at least ten minutes, and was careful not to "flip" them in the pan until they were set. Fefinitely needed the mayo, tomato and lettuce! Added strips of crispy bacon to the "burger" and that helped with the bland texture. Could also be served with chipotle sauce for more flavor. Will make again once I figure out to eliminate some of the liquids. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Very tasty! I used regular bread crumbs and added some basil to the mix. I also skipped the chili sauce and dill and added a bit of dijon.
It is a very soft mixture. I recommend coating the patties with cornmeal and refridgerating them before cooking. I cooked them on a George Foreman grill, which worked very well.

This is a super easy great and tasty recipe! I didn't have the red peppers or celery when I made it so I only used onion. Instead of bread crumbs I decided to crush some white cheddar Cheez-Its and it turned out great, lots of flavor.

A great change-up to boring ol' plain tuna patties. Really liked the addition of bell pepper, Worcestershire sauce, and dried dill (which really added a nice flavor). I did add some smoked paprika, as well as coat the outside in panko breadcrumbs seasoned with a few spices and parmesan cheese which was greatp The patties were a bit on the delicate side. Next time I might add a some more panko to the mix so they firm up a little more But, these were the best tuna patties I've had. Definitely am going to make these again

I add Old Bay Seasoning. After frying, we squeeze some fresh lemon juice on the patties. Delicious on whole wheat or pumpernickel buns. Makes a tasty Fish Friday supper with spiced roasted potato wedges.
These burgers are very tasty. My family loved them. I found that sauteing the veggies before adding them to the other ingredients worked best for me. This recipe is a keeper.
An amazing dish!!!! My family loved it... I added Jamicain meat season to the dish...
I followed the recipe, delish!! We loved how light and delicate these were and yet, so much flavor! The chili sauce I used was sweet, wonderful!

I doubled the recipe to meal prep & throw some burgers in the freezer for future meals. I changed a couple things like instead of eggs, I had egg whites. I kept the onions but replaced the celery & peppers with diced carrots. I also didn't have Worcestershire sauce so I hoped soy sauce would work. I'd say these came out really yummy. I ate mine on an english muffin with pesto & feta cheese then sauteed some mushrooms. Definitely glad I meal prepped a batch! :)
I did not have all the ingredients, used what I had. Turned out very good. Net time I will make sure I have everything for the recipe. Good recipe for an easy and low cost meal.
I made these for the second time tonight. Instead of having them as sandwiches, I served them as patties with rice and a vegetable. They are delicious.
